newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van der Moolen buys back own shares.
newsitem.headline: Van der Moolen buys back own shares.

text.p: Securities trading firm Van der Moolen NV said on Thursday it had bought back about nine percent of its outstanding ordinary shares.
The company said it had also placed 216,000 preference shares, representing about six percent of its total share capital, with an unnamed institutional investor.
Van der Moolen said the two transactions were expected to have a favourable effect on its earnings per ordinary share.
The company said that following the buy-back and the placement it now had 3.43 million ordinary shares and 216,000 preference shares outstanding.
It said it would seek shareholders' approval to permanently withdraw the shares which it had bought back.
The price Van der Moolen paid in the buy-back and received for the preference shares was based on the average closing price of its ordinary shares during the last five bourse sessions.
The preference shares will pay a dividend which is derived from the yield on 10-year Dutch government bonds. There are no plans to list them on the bourse for the time being.
